title: Criticism of Sauter-Finegan and anti-intellectualism
summary: The band's critical reception hurt it; discussion of McCarthyism and John Hammond.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Let's talk about a specific instance.
When you and Bill Finnegan had your band, there was quite a bit of negative criticism about the band. Do you think
Did it hurt the success you might have had?

Oh, sure; very much so. Of course, the times were involved in that too. It was the beginning of the rock scene. It was a kind of curious mixture of hillbilly and African, but with the emphasis on anti-intellectualism that went with that time. I think I'd have to blame the anti-intellectualism on the critics. I don't know why they put such a high premium on these things.
That was the McCarthy period too, so it was all part of that, a general part of what was happening.
We have a McCarthy period today, we have a new one arising.
I suppose it could be; I never thought that McCarthy had anything
to do with it though. Do you really think so?

If you're talking about anti-intellectualism, you had the time when the Hollywood Ten was getting summoned before the House on Unamerican Activities Committee and a lot of artists and actors and actresses were really, I guess, intimidated.
